newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mutual fund assets top $3.39 trillion - survey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mutual fund assets top $3.39 trillion - survey.

text.p: The Investment Company Institute said on Friday the nation's 6,201 mutual funds had combined assets of $3.39 trillion at the end of October, 1996.
The institute said in a survey that stock funds had assets of $1.65 trillion, or 48.7 percent of all industry assets, and totaled 2,553 in number.
Net new cash flow to stock funds totaled $192.62 billion through October, compared with $97.51 billion through October 1995 and $128.33 billion for all of 1995, the ICI survey said.
The average monthly inflow for 1996 through October was 1.36 percent of total assets compared to 1.00 percent a month in 1995, 1.24 percent in 1994 and 1.74 percent in 1993.

Performance accounted for 42 percent of the growth in total net assets through October. Net new cash flow into existing funds accounted for 46 percent and the remainder was from cash flow into new funds, the survey said.

The survey also said that 84 percent of the fund shareholders are investing for retirement, with retirement assets invested in mutual funds reaching the $1 trillion level, or about 35.7 percent of the fund industry's total assets.
The institute's membership includes 6,126 mutual funds, 442 closed-end investment companies and 10 sponsors of unit investment trusts.
